scope.methodology: Ranking question over eight working conditions; mean rank reported; n=5,204 for this item, distinct from the full sample of 12,684; self-selected non-representative sample
scope.setting: German hospital and long-term care nursing; online questionnaire
scope.who: Part-time and former (exited) nurses in hospital and long-term care who answered the eight-condition ranking question

findings.statement: In the autumn 2021 German online survey of part-time and former hospital and long-term-care nurses, Table 3 assigns reliable working times ('Verlässliche Arbeitszeiten') and higher pay to the second of four rank groups derived from eight working conditions. Reliable working times has mean rank 3.32; the ranking question has n=5,204, distinct from the full survey sample of 12,684. The sample is self-selected and not representative. This is evidence of respondents' desired conditions for return or increased hours, not current workforce prevalence, observed contact during time off, unrecorded overtime or actual return-to-work behaviour.
findings.title: Reliable working time in second rank group of eight conditions for return or increased hours (German nursing survey, autumn 2021)
findings.review_reason: Attached passages justify the finding within its stated scope. Table 3 caption (passage-d9e60d3f681235ae0d19d867) labels the ranking of the most important working conditions for re-entry and hour increase; the row "Verlässliche Arbeitszeiten 3,32" (passage-4be3c481c9b1e460cd803541 / passage-4fe169eb9e7fb60140c93767) and "Höhere Bezahlung 3,07" (passage-6781ea4cba6d0a7852e5c4dc) sit in the second rank group, with "Mehr Zeit für eine gute Pflege durch mehr Personal 2,15" (passage-9ea025a328c585d4a98f94f3) first and the surrounding text (passage-cc667b3dd8a897288901234f, passage-f51057e722173ce641927d8e, passage-64c3a183813ad5b83d4a3a01) describing four stable rank groups. The item n=5,204 (passage-21cac35087c7f109ba82ea5d) is correctly distinguished from the full sample of 12,684 (passage-682dea9c54141c009f8f7807), and the self-selected non-representative limitation is disclosed (passage-7223a3deb1c894ffd9b585c4). The finding appropriately frames this as relative importance for return/increased hours, not prevalence or actual return behaviour. Minor caveat: the "second of four rank groups" phrasing is interpretive (mean-rank grouping), but the scope already flags that the second rank group is not ordinal second place, so no material overreach. No price/admission/access condition applies to this survey finding.

scope.limitations: Historical short report; self-selection; subgroup ambiguity unresolved; no percentage or item denominator asserted; desired conditions do not establish actual care time, staffing, uptake or outcomes
scope.methodology: Online self-selected non-representative survey; thematic importance ratings; Table 4 subgroup labels conflict between surrounding text and source footer
scope.setting: German hospital and long-term care nursing; online questionnaire
scope.who: Part-time and former hospital/long-term-care nurses in the overall survey; exact Table 4 subgroup unresolved (source footer says exited nurses, surrounding text says joint presentation)

findings.statement: The April 2022 short report of the autumn 2021 German online nursing survey includes more time for human attention ('Mehr Zeit für menschliche Zuwendung') among the ten most important desired working conditions for return or increased hours. The surrounding text describes the ten conditions as identical for part-time and former nurses, differing slightly in order. Table 4's source footer instead labels the respondents as former nurses, so the subgroup for its numerical ratings remains unresolved here; no percentage or item denominator is asserted. The overall survey contains 12,684 evaluable responses from a self-selected, non-representative sample of part-time and former hospital and long-term-care nurses. Desired conditions do not establish current workforce prevalence, actual time available for care, staffing or outcomes.
findings.title: Time for human attention among the ten most important conditions for return or increased hours (German nursing survey, autumn 2021)
findings.review_reason: Attached passages justify the statement within its declared scope. passage-0a23f6f00696cfabf016feec shows item 6 "Mehr Zeit für menschliche Zuwendung" at 92.7% (n=7.730); passage-456d9ef91778a3d03fdbc943 and passage-51fe851b3390ac64fac1e964 supply the Table 4 caption ("Die zehn wichtigsten Arbeitsbedingungen für Rückkehr bzw. Stundenerhöhung"). The subgroup conflict is real and preserved, not resolved: passage-934fe7d54bf013f6c3b2d33a states the ten conditions are identical for both groups with only slightly differing order, while the footer (passage-12c30a8530432078d27f2fc5) labels respondents as exited nurses (n=6.612–7.707). Methodology/sample are correctly bounded: autumn 2021 fieldwork and 12,684 evaluable responses (passage-682dea9c54141c009f8f7807), explicitly self-selected and non-representative (passage-7223a3deb1c894ffd9b585c4), item n varying by question. The finding asserts no percentage or item denominator, keeps candidate/hypothesis status, and correctly notes desired conditions do not establish prevalence, actual care time or outcomes. Title matches the scoped claim with no inflation beyond the sample. No material condition or denominator gap remains unaddressed.
